source_title: Peloton (PTON) reports Q4 2022 losses mount (CNBC) - inventory overhang and cash burn
publisher_issuer: Peloton Interactive, Inc. (FY2022 Form 10-K and Q4 FY2022 results, filed with the SEC); reported by CNBC
company_context: Peloton over-built connected-fitness hardware capacity during the pandemic demand spike, then faced a sharp demand reversal that left excess and obsolete inventory and severe negative cash flow, straining working capital. SUBSTITUTION NOTE: used as the working-capital-stress case because it has explicit SEC-disclosed excess-inventory reserves and cash-burn figures that directly evidence working-capital and cash-conversion deterioration, in place of a generic DSO disclosure that could not be verbatim-verified.
business_type: Connected-fitness hardware plus subscription; inventory-heavy with long supply lead times and a fast-reversing demand curve
company_size_stage: public growth company past peak demand, in turnaround/cash-preservation
geography: United States headquartered; primarily North America revenue
time_period: fiscal year 2022 (year ended June 30, 2022), reported August 25, 2022
macro_context: Post-pandemic reopening collapsed at-home fitness demand after pandemic-era over-ordering, while rising rates raised the cost of funding negative free cash flow.
outcome_category: 7 - cash crisis / working-capital and liquidity strain
evidence_summary: Peloton's fiscal 2022 results show acute working-capital and cash strain from over-built inventory meeting collapsing demand: the company recorded excess and obsolete inventory reserve adjustments of about $224.9 million in fiscal 2022, and inventory decreased by about $398.6 million as a change in operating assets as it worked down the overhang. It burned about $412 million of cash in fiscal Q4 2022 after averaging roughly negative $650 million of cash flow in each of the prior two quarters, and ended June 2022 with about $1.25 billion of cash plus a $500 million revolving credit facility. It marked Peloton's sixth consecutive quarter of reported losses. The case is working-capital stress driven by inventory-to-demand mismatch and cash-conversion deterioration.

source_backed_metrics.consecutive_loss_quarters: sixth consecutive quarter of reported losses

owner_decision_context: Management had committed to large inventory and capacity buys to meet pandemic-era demand; when demand reversed, leadership had to choose between liquidating overstock at a loss to free cash and preserving runway via the credit facility.
action_taken: Recognized about $224.9 million of excess/obsolete inventory reserves, worked inventory down by about $398.6 million, cut costs, and relied on about $1.25 billion cash plus a $500 million revolver to fund continued large cash burn during the turnaround.
outcome_evidence: About $224.9 million inventory reserve, an approximately $398.6 million inventory drawdown, roughly $412-650 million quarterly cash burn, and six consecutive loss quarters against about $1.25 billion cash confirm working-capital and cash-conversion stress driven by inventory-demand mismatch.
source_limitations: WebFetch of CNBC and sec.gov returns HTTP 403 here; figures verified from search snippets of Peloton's FY2022 10-K / Q4 results and CNBC rather than full-text read. The reserve and inventory-change figures are GAAP working-capital line items, not a single DSO/cash-conversion-cycle number; the working-capital deterioration is evidenced through inventory reserves and cash burn (substitution noted).
directly_stated: Excess and obsolete inventory reserve adjustments of about $224.9 million in fiscal 2022
Inventory decreased by about $398.6 million as a change in operating assets
About $412 million cash burned in Q4 fiscal 2022 after roughly negative $650 million per quarter in the prior two quarters
Ended June 2022 with about $1.25 billion cash and a $500 million revolving credit facility; sixth consecutive loss quarter
inferred: The working-capital stress was driven by an inventory-to-demand mismatch tying up and then writing down cash
Cash conversion deteriorated as inventory built ahead of collapsing demand, forcing reserves and liquidation
why_useful_for_opsiq: Working-capital-stress case (thin category) with hard SEC figures. Tests whether OpsIQ identifies working_capital_stress and cash-conversion deterioration from inventory-demand mismatch, distinct from pure inventory_forecasting_mismatch or a demand failure, and triggers adaptive re-evaluation on cash burn and KPI deterioration.
